'self-settings':
      '---
name: self-settings
description: >
  Configure fa (flutter_agent_harness) itself by editing the exact config
  files the CLI settings commands write: provider/model selection and roles,
  memory paths, tool availability, cubes, MCP servers, redaction, skills
  access, approval and mode, themes and TUI appearance (tui.theme: switch
  or create a theme). Use when asked to reconfigure fa without a human
  in the REPL ("switch us to provider X", "point project memory at this
  path", "disable web_search for this project", "switch the theme to
  ohmypi").
when_to_use: Reconfiguring fa itself — settings, provider, models, memory,
  tools, cubes, MCP, redaction, skills access, themes/TUI appearance — on
  any host (CLI headless, REPL, app), by editing the YAML config the CLI
  persists (themes also via ~/.fah/themes/*.json), never by guessing keys.
argument-hint: "[what to configure, e.g. 'point project memory at ./memory']"
allowed-tools:
  - read
  - write
  - edit
  - ls
  - bash
  - config
user-invocable: true
disable-model-invocation: false
---

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls

💡 **SUGGESTION: replace the `uri.pathSegments.reversed.toList()[1]` basename idiom**

The name extraction relies on `Directory.uri` appending a trailing empty path segment so that `reversed[1]` is the directory name:

```dart
(d) => d.uri.pathSegments.reversed.toList()[1],
```

It works on POSIX and Windows today, but it is fragile and now duplicated in three places (`verify_builtin_skills.dart:88`, `verify_builtin_skills.dart:153`, and the byte-identical test at `builtin_skill_packaging_guard_test.dart:173` — plus the same idiom in `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`). A `basename`-style helper (e.g. `p.basename(d.path)` from `package:path`, already a transitive dep) would state the intent directly and give the four call sites one definition to stay consistent with `gen_prompts.dart`.

💡 **SUGGESTION: extract the duplicated gate step into a composite action**

The same five-line step (comment block + `dart pub get` + `dart run scripts/verify_builtin_skills.dart`) is now copied into five jobs across `build-mobile.yml` (×3), `build-macos.yml`, and `pages.yml`. This mirrors the existing gh-798 pattern, so it is consistent with the codebase — but any future tweak to the gate invocation (extra arg, different reporter format, caching of `pub get`) has to be edited in five places and can silently drift. A `.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills/action.yml` composite action would keep the invocation single-sourced; the gh-798 "Assert TestFlight version floor" step has the same shape and could migrate with it.

## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: The gh-1275 AC3 packaging-content gate is well-targeted and verified locally: `dart run scripts/verify_builtin_skills.dart` exits 0 on this tree, and all 13 tests in `test/skills/builtin_skill_packaging_guard_test.dart` pass, including the incident-shaped RED fixtures (dirs present, SKILL.md missing/empty). Workflow steps are placed after Flutter setup in every job, use pinned actions' `dart`, and assert before any build minute is spent.

**Key Issues**: None blocking. Three suggestions: a double file read / TOCTOU in `builtinSkillSourceViolations`, the fragile duplicated `uri.pathSegments.reversed[1]` basename idiom, and the 5× copied gate step that could become a composite action.

**Next Steps**:
1. (optional) Read each SKILL.md once via `readAsBytes` in the source checker
2. (optional) Extract a shared basename helper for skill-dir name resolution
3. (optional) Move the gate step into a composite action if it grows
4. AC1/AC2 (TestFlight/Play/macOS/web end-to-end) still require a human release carrying this gate — the gate proves the compiled artifact is non-hollow, not that a shipped build renders skills invocable

## PR Description

## gh-1275 — Built-in skills must ship CONTENT, not just directory structure

### Root Cause
- 1.0.512's app-side skill delivery (#1151) seeded `.fah/skills/` from bundled Flutter assets; the packaging never packed the SKILL.md content (same asset-diet class as #1227/#1272), so apps shipped skill DIRECTORY STRUCTURE with no usable content and the agent had no built-in skills on iOS.
- The mechanism half is already fixed in tree (gh-1164): every `prompts/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is compiled into pure-Dart `builtinSkillFiles` by `scripts/gen_prompts.dart` and served from `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` on every host — no asset-bundle/filesystem dependency, merged last into discovery, never gated by the skills-access consent (AC4 intact, covered by `test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart`).
- The missing half was the never-again hook: no release-gating check asserted SKILL.md CONTENT (byte size), only structure/wiring presence.

### Fix
- `scripts/verify_builtin_skills.dart` (new): the gh-1275 AC3 gate — flags empty/whitespace/frontmatter-only SKILL.md copies (1024-byte floor), skill dirs without SKILL.md, and packaged-vs-source name/byte drift; exit 1 with named `::error::` verdicts.
- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, `pages.yml`: fail-fast `Assert built-in skills packaged (gh-1275 AC3)` step in the iOS, Android (AAB + APK flavors), macOS, and web build jobs, before any build minute is spent (gh-798 "Assert TestFlight version floor" pattern).
- `test/skills/builtin_skill_packaging_guard_test.dart` (new): the same checkers run on every PR (gh-798 selftest pattern — the gate cannot rot silently), including RED fixtures shaped exactly like the incident (dirs present, content missing).
- `AGENTS.md`: retired the stale "js-apps seeds into `.fah/skills/` on startup" line (gh-1164 removed the seeder).

### Test Coverage
- `builtin_skill_packaging_guard_test.dart` — 13 tests: incident-shaped fixtures fail the gate (empty SKILL.md, dir without SKILL.md, stubs below the floor, parity drift), the real compiled `builtinSkillFiles` passes byte-identical to sources. PASS.
- `dart run scripts/verify_builtin_skills.dart` — exit 0 on the tree; exit 1 with named verdicts on a hollow fixture tree. VERIFIED.
- `test/skills/` + `test/prompts/` — 120 tests PASS. Full core suite: no regressions.

### Notes
- AC1/AC2 (verify TestFlight/Play/macOS/web builds end-to-end) still need a human release carrying this gate — the packaging path is shared pure-Dart compiled-in data, so the gate failing in any workflow proves the artifact is hollow before it ships.
- The cleanup in `_seedBundledSkills` intentionally leaves empty leftover dirs on upgraded devices; they are invisible to discovery (`_scanSkillDirs` skips dirs without SKILL.md) and harmless.

## Description

**Evidence** (owner, iOS fa 1.0.512 / TestFlight build 205, session clip_1791193461546.txt, 2026-10-05): user asks the agent «есть ли у тебя скилл как писать js apps и как create goal делать?» → the agent discovers the skill DIRECTORIES exist (`create-goal`, `fa-self-config`, `js-apps` listed) but are EMPTY — «The skill directories exist but are empty. Check maybe SKILL.md is elsewhere?» — so the agent has no usable built-in skills on iOS.

**Shape**: #1151 shipped built-in skills with fa; the app bundling copies/creates the skill directory STRUCTURE but not the SKILL.md CONTENT (or the packaging glob misses .md assets). Owner suspects other platforms are equally affected — macOS/Android/**web** builds need the same check; the CLI (repo-adjacent) works.

**Never-again hook**: this is the same packaging-blindness class as #1227's asset diet — shipped-shape verification must assert CONTENT, not directory presence: a release-gating check that each built-in skill dir contains a non-empty SKILL.md (byte size > some floor) in the packaged artifact.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: on iOS, the app's agent sees and can invoke the built-in skills (create-goal, fa-self-config, js-apps) — verified on a TestFlight build carrying the fix.
- AC2: FULL platform matrix (owner directive — every platform): iOS, Android, macOS, web (fa1.dev), and desktop CLI — built-in skills visible and invocable on each; no platform skipped without a written reason (or explicitly excluded with a written reason).
- AC3: packaging regression guard: the release workflow fails if any built-in skill dir ships without a non-empty SKILL.md.
- AC4: skills remain inert-by-default security-wise (discovery respects the skills-access setting on all platforms).

Unassigned per owner. Refs: #1151, #1227 (asset-packaging class), #1272 (the sibling 1.0.512 packaging incident).

name: self-settings
description: >

  files the CLI settings commands write: provider/model selection and roles,
  memory paths, tool availability, cubes, MCP servers, redaction, skills

  or create a theme). Use when asked to reconfigure fa without a human
  in the REPL ("switch us to provider X", "point project memory at this
  path", "disable web_search for this project", "switch the theme to
  ohmypi").
when_to_use: Reconfiguring fa itself — settings, provider, models, memory,
  tools, cubes, MCP, redaction, skills access, themes/TUI appearance — on
  any host (CLI headless, REPL, app), by editing the YAML config the CLI
  persists (themes also via ~/.fah/themes/*.json), never by guessing keys.
argument-hint: "[what to configure, e.g. 'point project memory at ./memory']"
allowed-tools:
  - read
  - write
  - edit
  - ls
  - bash
  - config
user-invocable: true
disable-model-invocation: false
---

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the…

## PR Description

## gh-1275 — Built-in skills must ship CONTENT, not just directory structure

### Root Cause
- 1.0.512's app-side skill delivery (#1151) seeded `.fah/skills/` from bundled Flutter assets; the packaging never packed the SKILL.md content (same asset-diet class as #1227/#1272), so apps shipped skill DIRECTORY STRUCTURE with no usable content and the agent had no built-in skills on iOS.
- The mechanism half is already fixed in tree (gh-1164): every `prompts/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is compiled into pure-Dart `builtinSkillFiles` by `scripts/gen_prompts.dart` and served from `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` on every host — no asset-bundle/filesystem dependency, merged last into discovery, never gated by the skills-access consent (AC4 intact, covered by `test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart`).
- The missing half was the never-again hook: no release-gating check asserted SKILL.md CONTENT (byte size), only structure/wiring presence.

### Fix
- `scripts/verify_builtin_skills.dart` (new): the gh-1275 AC3 gate — flags empty/whitespace/frontmatter-only SKILL.md copies (1024-byte floor), skill dirs without SKILL.md, and packaged-vs-source name/byte drift; exit 1 with named `::error::` verdicts.
- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, `pages.yml`: fail-fast `Assert built-in skills packaged (gh-1275 AC3)` step in the iOS, Android (AAB + APK flavors), macOS, and web build jobs, before any build minute is spent (gh-798 "Assert TestFlight version floor" pattern).
- `test/skills/builtin_skill_packaging_guard_test.dart` (new): the same checkers run on every PR (gh-798 selftest pattern — the gate cannot rot silently), including RED fixtures shaped exactly like the incident (dirs present, content missing).
- `AGENTS.md`: retired the stale "js-apps seeds into `.fah/skills/` on startup" line (gh-1164 removed the seeder).

### Test Coverage
- `builtin_skill_packaging_guard_test.dart` — 13 tests: incident-shaped fixtures fail the gate (empty SKILL.md, dir without SKILL.md, stubs below the floor, parity drift), the real compiled `builtinSkillFiles` passes byte-identical to sources. PASS.
- `dart run scripts/verify_builtin_skills.dart` — exit 0 on the tree; exit 1 with named verdicts on a hollow fixture tree. VERIFIED.
- `test/skills/` + `test/prompts/` — 120 tests PASS. Full core suite: no regressions.

### Notes
- AC1/AC2 (verify TestFlight/Play/macOS/web builds end-to-end) still need a human release carrying this gate — the packaging path is shared pure-Dart compiled-in data, so the gate failing in any workflow proves the artifact is hollow before it ships.
- The cleanup in `_seedBundledSkills` intentionally leaves empty leftover dirs on upgraded devices; they are invisible to discovery (`_scanSkillDirs` skips dirs without SKILL.md) and harmless.

'self-settings':
      '---
name: self-settings
description: >
  Configure fa (flutter_agent_harness) itself by editing the exact config
  files the CLI settings commands write: provider/model selection and roles,
  memory paths, tool availability, cubes, MCP servers, redaction, skills
  access, approval and mode, themes and TUI appearance (tui.theme: switch
  or create a theme). Use when asked to reconfigure fa without a human
  in the REPL ("switch us to provider X", "point project memory at this
  path", "disable web_search for this project", "switch the theme to
  ohmypi").
when_to_use: Reconfiguring fa itself — settings, provider, models, memory,
  tools, cubes, MCP, redaction, skills access, themes/TUI appearance — on
  any host (CLI headless, REPL, app), by editing the YAML config the CLI
  persists (themes also via ~/.fah/themes/*.json), never by guessing keys.
argument-hint: "[what to configure, e.g. 'point project memory at ./memory']"
allowed-tools:
  - read
  - write
  - edit
  - ls
  - bash
  - config
user-invocable: true
disable-model-invocation: false
---

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the…

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1275` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T11:07:55Z

## PR Description

## gh-1275 — Built-in skills must ship CONTENT, not just directory structure

### Root Cause
- 1.0.512's app-side skill delivery (#1151) seeded `.fah/skills/` from bundled Flutter assets; the packaging never packed the SKILL.md content (same asset-diet class as #1227/#1272), so apps shipped skill DIRECTORY STRUCTURE with no usable content and the agent had no built-in skills on iOS.
- The mechanism half is already fixed in tree (gh-1164): every `prompts/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is compiled into pure-Dart `builtinSkillFiles` by `scripts/gen_prompts.dart` and served from `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` on every host — no asset-bundle/filesystem dependency, merged last into discovery, never gated by the skills-access consent (AC4 intact, covered by `test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart`).
- The missing half was the never-again hook: no release-gating check asserted SKILL.md CONTENT (byte size), only structure/wiring presence.

### Fix
- `scripts/verify_builtin_skills.dart` (new): the gh-1275 AC3 gate — flags empty/whitespace/frontmatter-only SKILL.md copies (1024-byte floor), skill dirs without SKILL.md, and packaged-vs-source name/byte drift; exit 1 with named `::error::` verdicts.
- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, `pages.yml`: fail-fast `Assert built-in skills packaged (gh-1275 AC3)` step in the iOS, Android (AAB + APK flavors), macOS, and web build jobs, before any build minute is spent (gh-798 "Assert TestFlight version floor" pattern).
- `test/skills/builtin_skill_packaging_guard_test.dart` (new): the same checkers run on every PR (gh-798 selftest pattern — the gate cannot rot silently), including RED fixtures shaped exactly like the incident (dirs present, content missing).
- `AGENTS.md`: retired the stale "js-apps seeds into `.fah/skills/` on startup" line (gh-1164 removed the seeder).

### Test Coverage
- `builtin_skill_packaging_guard_test.dart` — 13 tests: incident-shaped fixtures fail the gate (empty SKILL.md, dir without SKILL.md, stubs below the floor, parity drift), the real compiled `builtinSkillFiles` passes byte-identical to sources. PASS.
- `dart run scripts/verify_builtin_skills.dart` — exit 0 on the tree; exit 1 with named verdicts on a hollow fixture tree. VERIFIED.
- `test/skills/` + `test/prompts/` — 120 tests PASS. Full core suite: no regressions.

### Notes
- AC1/AC2 (verify TestFlight/Play/macOS/web builds end-to-end) still need a human release carrying this gate — the packaging path is shared pure-Dart compiled-in data, so the gate failing in any workflow proves the artifact is hollow before it ships.
- The cleanup in `_seedBundledSkills` intentionally leaves empty leftover dirs on upgraded devices; they are invisible to discovery (`_scanSkillDirs` skips dirs without SKILL.md) and harmless.

# gh-1275: [BUG] Built-in skills (#1151) not packaged into the apps: iOS ships EMPTY skill dirs (create-goal/fa-self-config/js-apps exist, SKILL.md missing) — verify macOS/Android too

## Description

**Evidence** (owner, iOS fa 1.0.512 / TestFlight build 205, session clip_1791193461546.txt, 2026-10-05): user asks the agent «есть ли у тебя скилл как писать js apps и как create goal делать?» → the agent discovers the skill DIRECTORIES exist (`create-goal`, `fa-self-config`, `js-apps` listed) but are EMPTY — «The skill directories exist but are empty. Check maybe SKILL.md is elsewhere?» — so the agent has no usable built-in skills on iOS.

**Shape**: #1151 shipped built-in skills with fa; the app bundling copies/creates the skill directory STRUCTURE but not the SKILL.md CONTENT (or the packaging glob misses .md assets). Owner suspects other platforms are equally affected — macOS/Android/**web** builds need the same check; the CLI (repo-adjacent) works.

**Never-again hook**: this is the same packaging-blindness class as #1227's asset diet — shipped-shape verification must assert CONTENT, not directory presence: a release-gating check that each built-in skill dir contains a non-empty SKILL.md (byte size > some floor) in the packaged artifact.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: on iOS, the app's agent sees and can invoke the built-in skills (create-goal, fa-self-config, js-apps) — verified on a TestFlight build carrying the fix.
- AC2: FULL platform matrix (owner directive — every platform): iOS, Android, macOS, web (fa1.dev), and desktop CLI — built-in skills visible and invocable on each; no platform skipped without a written reason (or explicitly excluded with a written reason).
- AC3: packaging regression guard: the release workflow fails if any built-in skill dir ships without a non-empty SKILL.md.
- AC4: skills remain inert-by-default security-wise (discovery respects the skills-access setting on all platforms).

Unassigned per owner. Refs: #1151, #1227 (asset-packaging class), #1272 (the sibling 1.0.512 packaging incident).

name: self-settings
description: >
  Configure fa (flutter_agent_harness) itself by editing the exact config
  files the CLI settings commands write: provider/model selection and roles,
  memory paths, tool availability, cubes, MCP servers, redaction, skills
  access, approval and mode, themes and TUI appearance (tui.theme: switch
  or create a theme). Use when asked to reconfigure fa without a human
  in the REPL ("switch us to provider X", "point project memory at this
  path", "disable web_search for this project", "switch the theme to
  ohmypi").
when_to_use: Reconfiguring fa itself — settings, provider, models, memory,
  tools, cubes, MCP, redaction, skills access, themes/TUI appearance — on
  any host (CLI headless, REPL, app), by editing the YAML config the CLI
  persists (themes also via ~/.fah/themes/*.json), never by guessing keys.
argument-hint: "[what to configure, e.g. 'point project memory at ./memory']"
allowed-tools:
  - read
  - write
  - edit
  - ls
  - bash
  - config
user-invocable: true
disable-model-invocation: false
---

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the…
